reason: This text from Genesis 29-31 describes personal disputes between Jacob and Laban rather than collective suffering of the Hebrew people with communal leaders assigning blame. While Laban accuses Jacob of wrongdoing (stealing his heart and household idols), there is no instance where a leader tells a people that their suffering is self-inflicted. The narrative focuses on individual family conflicts and business disputes, with Jacob defending his conduct by recounting his labors and hardships (31:40), but Laban never frames Jacob's sufferings as consequences of Jacob's own faults or sins. The text lacks both the communal dimension (the 'Hebrew people' as a collective) and the blame-assignment pattern that the statement describes.
